Building a cedar canoe

By Ana Ruiz

It started with a stack of western red cedar that a neighbor no longer needed. Three winters later, the canoe floats, and it floats straight, which is more than I expected when I glued the first strip to the forms in the garage.

The forms came first. Station molds cut from plywood, screwed to a strongback, each one checked twice against the table of offsets. Getting them fair took longer than any other single step, and every hour spent there paid back later when the strips lay down without a fight.

Fiberglass and epoxy came last. The first coat soaked in unevenly, the second was better, and the third looked like glass. If you are thinking about building one, start with the forms, take your time, and keep the garage warm.

Next spring the canoe goes to the lake for its first real trip, and I already have a list of things I would do differently on the second boat, starting with the thwarts and the seats.
